correctness.rationale: The exact domain is 16 binary vertices with generators {1,2,4,8,15}, and 4-flips are the only allowed transitions. A least-uncovered-vertex recurrence partitions all perfect matchings and finds 705, independently reproduced in Python and C++. A constructive cross-pairing flip enumeration agrees edge-for-edge with exhaustive 705-choose-2 symmetric differences. Every source BFS visits all 705 matchings; counts yield 2160 flips, eccentricity multiplicities {7:5,8:700}, diameter 8, radius 7 and 8840 unordered diameter pairs. 16 translations and all 120 generator permutations give the entire automorphism group of order 1920; exhaustive actions on every configuration produce the seven named orbits with direction patterns, degrees and eccentricities. The two checker source files compile and execute on their own; no infinite-family inference or extrapolation is involved.

originality.rationale: The full 705-state alternating-quadrilateral flip graph is explicitly and exhaustively classified: 2160 moves, radius seven, diameter eight, five unique parallel-direction centers, seven orbits under the complete 1920-element automorphism group. The known scalar 705 matching count and the known exact prescribed-direction multiplicities are excluded from the novelty claim. The accessible published records supply no adjacency, all-pairs distances, or full-automorphism orbit decomposition; established switch-chain results give general reconfiguration theory, not these exact strongly-regular-graph invariants. Aliases and implication-level comparisons were searched. Residual risk of independent unindexed enumeration remains.
residual_risks: An exact same finite computation might be published under folded-cube, Greenwood–Gleason, projective-cube, or switch-chain terminology in unindexed or inaccessible sources.

value.rationale: The Clebsch graph is the canonical 16-vertex, five-regular triangle-free strongly regular graph, and perfect matchings are basic combinatorial feasible solutions. The previously known number 705 does not describe whether one optimal pairing can be continuously exchanged for another. Exact connectedness, sharp 8-move worst-case transition, five canonical centers, and seven full symmetry types distinguish combinatorial accessibility and intrinsic geometry of the solution space, providing a reproducible benchmark for 4-cycle-flip chains. These are naturally motivated invariants of this standard graph, not an arbitrary restricted sample.
